item.title: Prewar US business cycles under uncertainty: reconstructing quarterly GDP before 1947
item.description: Official quarterly US GDP estimates begin in 1947; earlier quarterly histories must be reconstructed using annual benchmarks and historical indicators. To investigate uncertainty in these reconstructions, this paper systematically compares specifications drawn from the literature for reconstructing quarterly GDP during 1919–1946. The comparison evaluates predictions on concealed postwar quarters and separates variation across specifications from coefficient uncertainty within a model.
item.dc:title: Prewar US business cycles under uncertainty: reconstructing quarterly GDP before 1947
item.dc:creator: Raphael Auer

item.title: News shocks and inflation: theory and evidence from large oil discoveries
item.description: We study how news shocks affect inflation in open economies, using large oil and gas discoveries with realized production lags of at least five years as observable news about future output. Panel local projections show that discoveries raise core consumer prices over the subsequent decade, with about half the increase occurring prior to extraction.

item.title: Bank liquidity regulation and the growth of private credit
item.description: We study the role of bank liquidity regulation in the growth of private credit. Following the introduction of the liquidity coverage ratio (LCR), private credit increases significantly more in U.S. counties with a larger footprint of banks subject to the LCR or of LCR banks with greater initial liquidity shortfalls.

item.title: Offshore forwards and exchange rate transmission in emerging markets
item.description: We study how offshore non-deliverable forward (NDF) markets transmit exchange-rate pressures to domestic currency markets. Using unique transaction-level data on the universe of centrally cleared NDFs for ten emerging-market currencies over 2013–2025, we show that offshore NDF order flow moves both offshore forward and domestic spot exchange rates and widens the offshore–onshore forward spread.

item.title: Are stablecoins and bank deposits substitutes?
item.description: We test whether stablecoins and bank deposits act as substitutes by estimating the semi-elasticity of stablecoin market capitalization with respect to deposit rate changes. Using local projections fit to weekly U.S. data from January 2019 to June 2025, we find that deposit rate increases predict slower stablecoin growth. To address endogeneity, we exploit a nonlinearity in deposit rate pass-through.

item.title: Chasing El Dorado: gold under shifting geopolitical and financial conditions
item.description: This paper analyses the state-dependent effects of geopolitical risks on gold prices (i.e. the safe-haven role of gold), conditional on financial conditions. Geopolitical risks are often associated with tighter financial conditions. However, recent data reveal a decoupling between such shocks and more restrictive financial conditions, raising the question of how gold returns are affected by geopolitical shocks, conditional on the macro-financial environment.

item.title: Settlement liquidity in the Colombian large-value payment system: the role of reserve requirements
item.description: This paper analyzes the intraday timing of transactions in Colombia's large-value payment system (CUD) from 2018 to 2025, focusing on how changes in reserve requirements affect liquidity management by financial institutions. Using high-frequency transaction data, we document that reductions in reserve requirements in April 2020 and September 2024 are associated with a shift of settlement activity toward later hours of the day.
